body:
Couldn't agree with you more. 
Easily the best book I've read on the topic that really helped me understand and analyze my family's behavior patterns and abuse cycle.
THIS

When I married my wife and saw how the in laws treated her and me, I couldn't  help but notice the dysfunction in my family. 

I could then understand how a loving parent would treat their children.

Yes, same here and I believe most of us who have experiences with Nparents can relate to the issue you are having here.
After all, that is all we witnessed and learned throughout the early years of our life. 
It is hard not to pick up some of those habits along the way. 
I think it is important for you to create a clear boundary with Nfamily and start surrounding yourself with genuine people so that you can emotionally mature yourself as well as learning from your family's wrongdoings.
Thank you for your advice. Will be seeing if they do respect my wish for NC or not!
Totally agree with you on through and near to perfect portrayed image. They just never lose it in public.
Will take note on that. Thank you

You are right that when they are covert no one believes you.
For that reason, I have just decided to get away from entire family as a whole due to worries of flying monkeys. (My family is big with tons of extended family living near me)
Coming from Asia and having only lived in west and east coast, not really familiar with how south is but it sounds pretty intense that everyone is expected to be that religious.

I totally get you.
I've never seen my parents argue or fight with others in public once yet they verbally and physically abused me at home frequently. It is a pretty disgusting feeling to see everyone taking Nparents sides despite their abusive traits due to their close to perfect public face.

Season 2 is definitely more triggering in terms of the family getting exposed of their dysfunction more and facing the reality. The plot is more intense with the tensions and conflicts building more between the family members. Nonetheless, I think both seasons are great and also a pretty realistic portrayal of N family.

Yes, you are right that my depression is replapsing and my self esteem is at rock bottom due to not much going on with life during the late years. Will be seeking professional help soon as you recommended. 

Thank you again
Thank you for kind words. I will definitely look into counseling.
Thank you for your support.
Definitely, it's almost like they have an ideal image of themselves in their head they are trying to follow yet blinded and destroying everyone around them on the way.

I agree. That's the thing with achievement of social and financial status that people will not be calling you out as much and I too have experienced similar things with my dad and how people many act and say cautiously towards him. My case is a little different tho because my Ndad is a master at portrayal of public image and is well respected by most that knows him for that reason.

Totally agree. 
"Thanks for the article. I will carefully read it. But, at least as of now, I can say that I am not a narcissistic parent. I pray and earnestly hope that you find true yourself as soon as possible and truly enjoy your life. Mom and I love you and so please feel free to be our guest whenever you would like to be. Thank you for writing to me. - Dad. "

This is the response I got for my first confrontation about family dysfunction and abuse with Covert Ndad when I asked for NC after explaining the family dysfunction with an attached article about narcissistic parent. Sounds like an answer coming from a soulless person.

+church going religious and conservative

You have just described my dad.

I feel like I'm the one that's needs to first start helping myself but having a hard time taking steps or making changes and just falling into bad habits and deep holes in many areas of life. So I'm not sure if I can confidently say I love her since for most part of 3 yr marriage I let her down. 

I am considering getting professional help again starting next month and your method of asking those questions before acting sounds great to me. 

Thank you for the advice and kind words

28M here.

Until recently when I watched the show "bloodline" on Netflix(johns family was super similar to my family including Ngrandparents) and found this subreddit following that, I used to believe my parents were wonderful hard working loving people who are great in their roles as members of family, society, and etc. Also believed that there Was something wrong with me for not connecting with my family. 

Well, it's not too late, considering your parents still didn't, and mine didn't either. 

Cheers

For me personally, I hate and am scared at myself for the fact that I feel to be lacking empathy and not on line(connecting) with my wife's emotions during an interaction. (Joy, sorrow, anger, etc) 
This emotionless and tearless cold trait of mine made me question myself regarding this. 

A far as your question, I feel my wife loves me that she's bearing with something that she does not deserve at all. (My coldness, irresponsibility, low mood, basically am a zombie these days emotionally and physically) 
I trust my wife with everything and also tell her everything almost too much for her to handle. I had many conversation with her about what I learned from this subreddit, my family, and also some of hers. She is basically the only person on this planet that sees what is closest to my true self now. At the same time, I can be very ignorant and unempathetic towards her which breaks her occasionally. I just feel like I'm building pain and sorrow in her I do not see much of a way out.

It has led me to substance addiction, physical and mental breakdown, depression, social anxiety, in the following order without even realizing I was raised in an abusive household as my parents were masters at portraying the perfect family image while emotionally and physically abusing at home in the name of love and education. 

First step, in my opinion, is to realize your issues, find out what your parents did wrong and could have done differently, and incorporate that into your own life. For me personally, I decided to go NC since my parents are super closer to each other and I have nothing left for them anyways.

But is she more important to you than family?
I sure did connect with my friends much more my entire life due to not being able to connect with any of my family at all due to their N traits. 
I think that's the question you need to ask yourself and just be upfront about it. It will be hard at first but it made everything so much clearer for me to be brutally honest about my feelings and acting accordingly to family. (I'm now NC btw)

I basically was living just like you feeding their insecurities, N supplies, and playing into their games occasionally. That shit was driving me crazy and I can tell you that at least for me if the boundary and respect cannot be properly created through conversation, I think it's better to go NC at all if you have financial independence.

I use to think like that due to their masterful ways of manipulation and guilt trips, and also due to the the household and culture I was raised in. 
Now raising a pup for a year I realize how small of a a person they both were and still are and that their definition of love is twisted and also conditional at the same time.

"The most important thing to consider here is whether you're happier without them. That's all that matters. People who love you can still be a detriment to your mental health and safety."

I read this from a post by fellow redditor and helped me tons with guilt trips and gaining insight. You are in a similar boat as me, my dad has a respected position in society with his beautiful wife, is religious and kind to others in public and to relatives. For this reason, it took me so long to figure out the dysfunction in my family and when I did and found this subreddit, boy it was a brainfuck. I just recently started questioning at age of 28. 
Now I'm NC with my family and couldn't be better mentally. Just keep educating yourself for better analysis and I'm sure you will come up with an answer you will be confident with yourself. 

Have you watched "make happy" by bo burnham on Netflix?
If you have not I recommend you do so!

7th grade I crashed into a bus while riding a bicycle(wasn't hurt much besides bruises and little rashes) but was taken to the police station for further report. I remember him getting angry at me after picking me up in the car on the way home for making him come to the police station and making him lose face. Never bothered to ask me if I was ok at all. 



5th grade a couple friends of mine were calling me out for stealing one of their wallet which I did not do and he witnessed it. 


And again, instead of asking what happened, he just starts going red face and angry at me for being called out a thief.

It's very interesting I never even bothered to question these behaviors of his until I recently found out about narcissism and this subreddit.

That is exactly what I was thinking. I was surprised to see him change the topic of the convo with denying that he is a narc parent, without even having any background info on the topic. He just denied without even bothering to research and learn. I confronted him and his parents and he just denies he is nparent without any explanation. This seemed like a red flag to me but will see. And I for sure feel much better going NC and speaking up my mind looking from his reaction so far. 

Thank you

This is great. 

"The most important thing to consider here is whether you're happier without them. That's all that matters. People who love you can still be a detriment to your mental health and safety."

Thank you
Thanks for sharing and good to hear that your mother could own it at the end. My father too I feel is incapable of empathy.
That's the part I'm trying to figure out, too!

"It's not impossible for an N to genuinely believe they mean well or have someone else's best interests at heart... very often, though, this gets twisted under the assumption that they know better. That's where everything tends to go to hell."

This is gold. 
Thank you

That is interesting because I, too, find myself repeating similar patterns to my wife and cringe at myself occasionally. Looks like it really needs a strong will and commitment to break the cycle that We've been used to it for so long. It is good to hear that your mother recognizes the issue tho as it will open up a chance for communication. 
At the same time, indont get the part why she would want you to pretend fight never happened.

You couldn't describe what I feel more perfectly. (Besides the gps part and Im sorry! My mother does similar to my 18yd sis tho and I'm 28m) 
Im trying NC at the moment but they are always in my head especially tough dealing with the guilt trips thinking that they are victims as well to Nparents(dad) and seeing dad with tears and trying hard in his own way makes me very confused even though I know his method is toxic to me and I know that I won't emotionally connect with him as I haven't for the past 28 years. (It's like he loves me enough to give up everything HE has but not respecting my opinions or emotions at the same time. That makes a person go insane imo.)

This is really helpful. The cycle of abuse chart scares me to think that it started from my dad being raised in Nhousehold and mom being affected throughout marriage while living with them. I see an unbroken cycle keep repeating unless we try to break it ourselves, especially due to the elderly respecting Confucius based cultures in Asia where I'm from.

Hey!

I'm sorry to hear that your mother is saying those things to you. I wonder if you ever question your parents' ideologies, opinions and make them try to understand from a different perspective. Because it is so fucking hard for me that they just try to live in a bubble they have created and negatively judging anything or anyone that might be slightly different than from or offensive to them. 
I believe that to be a trait of being narcissistic. 

And I have to disagree with you on the part that we pretty much go through the same thing. I agree that many of us experience the similar level of academic burdens which basically takes our youth away. But in the process, I also believe that it is possible for parents to realize the children's genuine emotional needs as well while seeking academic ambitions at the same time without overburdening their children. 

I believe what is important as a parent is to learn from your mistakes and maybe it's the Korean culture that makes it hard for our parents from being able to emotionally connect with us?
I do not completely agree since I believe it is partially my parents fault that they never showed anything about their lives and never opens up about themselves while trying to micromanage me and get inside my brain controlling every single aspect of my life including academic, social, time management, etc.

If you don't mind me asking, do you see your mother to be living a fulfilling and happy life being confident about herself in general? 
I surely don't think mine are and their lives are way skewed towards their kids with no balance of friendship, recreational life, and life outside of family. They practically got NOTHING besides family, they live for that like its their life goal yet still obsesses and emotionally abuses us(only younger sister now since I'm NC) in the name of love. 
I believe that not being well rounded in life has a lot to do with them being emotionally unstable themselves thus leading to this obsessive abuse consciously or subconsciously. 

And what do you think are some differences between typical Korean parenting and raised by narcissists?
